name: PUT /api/relationships/:relationship_id/scope — close by setting valid_to, never delete
description: The existing scope endpoint, extended so a relationship can be CLOSED by setting valid_to rather than terminated destructively. Proves AC2 and AC4. Closing keeps the row answering 'who was the carer last March' — precisely the question asked when something has gone wrong, and one a deleted row cannot answer. AC4 is preserved by the shape of the extension: closing is opt-in via close:true, and a body WITHOUT it takes the pre-existing scope/status path completely unchanged, so every current caller is unaffected. The close branch is evaluated before validateUpdateScope on purpose, because a close needs neither a scope nor a status and requiring one would force callers to send a field they do not mean. QA edge cases: closing is IDEMPOTENT — a retry or a double-click returns the row with its ORIGINAL valid_to and closed_reason rather than moving the date, since the first close is when the role actually stopped being true; a closed role leaves the live view but is still returned with include_closed=true, and the underlying row count is unchanged (verified directly); closing frees the (pair, kind, role_label) slot so the same role can legitimately be re-granted later, leaving both the historical and the new row; valid_to may be back-dated but a CHECK forbids it preceding valid_from; closed_reason cannot be set without a valid_to; an unknown relationship_id is 404.

testCases.name: Close a role by setting valid_to
Closing again is idempotent and keeps the original close date
The legacy scope-update path is unchanged

errorCases.name: A legacy body with neither scope nor status is still refused
errorCases.message: at least one of scope or status is required
errorCases.when: close is not set and the body carries neither scope nor status — unchanged from before this feature

errorCases.name: Unauthenticated is refused by the default-deny gate
errorCases.when: no valid tenant Bearer token on the request
